title: Neural Tier — Where It Stands
thesis: The consumption side is complete and genuinely wired to a patched, vendored ggml: real GGUF loading, id-exact tokenizers, a numpy-parity BERT encoder, a multi-architecture causal LLM decoder with grammar-constrained decoding, and a measurement-gated GPU path. What is not there is the production side. A llama.cpp-class runner, wired into a governed library — not yet a training or model-production platform.

lanes.note: neural_embed.zig loads GGUF metadata + weights into a ggml context; F16/Q8_0 de-quant on load; tested against a committed tiny_bert.gguf
WordPiece/SentencePiece-metaspace and GPT-2 byte-level BPE from the GGUF vocab; tokenization is id-exact against a numpy reference
Full BERT-family forward (MiniLM/BERT/RoBERTa/jina-bert-v2): embeddings, NER, rerank, matching an independent numpy reference to 1.64e-7
GBNF grammar-constrained decoding makes invalid tokens unemittable; ~5 calls per valid answer without the grammar, one with
llama/qwen2/qwen3/smollm with KV-cache, sampling, streaming; CI has no generative model, so proven by construction, not by a parity fixture
Vendored ggml tensor core wired; stzMatrix<->ggml bridge routes f64 matmul through ggml; the bridge is matmul-only, no backward pass
stzSemanticIndex AddText/Search over StzNeuralEmbeddingOf; shipped and tested, but the strong model is user-supplied (only tiny_bert.gguf tracked)
wgpu resident BERT backbone auto-routes to GPU via the calibration foundry: 2.08x on the backbone forward, 5.3x over full CPU forward; training sees no GPU
nn.zig forward + backward SGD for small dense MLPs (learns XOR, tested); no transformer training, ggml-opt.cpp vendored but never called
Consume-only: F16 and Q8_0 de-quantized on load (dequantRows); no encode path, GGUF export writes F32 only
gguf_export.zig writes GGUF for small F32 nets (stz-mlp, bigram DLM), round-trip verified; foundry rung 2 (train a transformer) is unbuilt
None: GGUF is the chosen and only model format; no ONNX import, runtime or export anywhere in the engine or faces

standouts: grammar-constrained decoding wired to the structured-output contract
gaps: wire ggml's backward pass -- the training foundry
ship or fetch a real semantic model for CI
